title: Adaptive microthread quota and deadline-aware batching for reranker
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The reranking endpoint has inconsistent tail latency under mixed workloads (short chat requests + long-document reranks). Current batching prioritizes throughput which causes occasional P99 spikes and unfair token starvation for latency-sensitive requests. Goal: implement an adaptive microthread quota allocator and deadline-aware batching that enforces per-request token caps, soft timeouts, and speculative parallelization for short candidates to reduce tail latency while preserving overall throughput and quality.

Scope:
- Implement token-based microthread quotas at the reranker dispatcher so each request gets a dynamic cap computed from request SLA, candidate size distribution, and global load.
- Add soft deadline semantics (soft_timeout_ms) propagated through the pipeline and honored by the scheduler and model runtime (graceful early-exit or reduced beam work).
- Deadline-aware batch formation: prefer mixing short-candidate requests with long ones only when quotas allow; create fast-path microbatches for sub-100-token candidates.
- KV-prefetch prioritization: prefetch keys for higher-priority/low-latency requests ahead of batching windows.
- Instrumentation & metrics: per-request allocated_tokens, tokens_consumed, soft_timeout_triggered, early_exit_rate, and P50/P95/P99 latency by request class.

Success metrics (target):
- Reduce rerank P99 latency for latency-sensitive class by >= 30% under 95th percentile load.
- Keep overall throughput degradation <= 10% for steady-state rerank load.
- Maintain quality regression <= 1% on evaluation set (rerank NDCG/Recall).

Design notes:
- The allocator uses a small moving-window estimator of token demand per request class and current free-token pool. Quota = min(max_tokens_per_request, fair_share * weight_by_sla). Weight_by_sla derived from route config.
- Soft timeout is a best-effort signal: runtime should try to finish current token and then emit the highest-confidence rerank scores; for autoregressive scorers, runtime returns partial logits and we compute scores on partial outputs.
- For long-candidate batches, we allow speculative parallel scoring across CPU-backed shallow scorers (quantized) to reduce blocking on single GPU microbatch.
- Safety: default quotas conservative; feature gated behind runtime flag rerank.adaptive_quota = true.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on staging with canary traffic flag (10% of test traffic) and full telemetry.
2) Internal beta: enable for non-critical customers (no SLA).
3) Incremental ramp by 10% weekly with health checks (latency, error rate, quality metrics).

Risk/mitigations:
- Quality regression: run eval harness on rerank gold set; keep fallback to current batching if quality drops >1%.
- Starvation of bulk jobs: implement max_global_tokens guarantee and long-job backpressure circuit.
- Scheduler complexity: keep allocator implementation modest; start with single-node estimator before distributed heuristics.

Open questions:
- Exact fairness function for mixed-priority workloads (linear vs. weighted).
- Best partial-scoring fallback for autoregressive encoders (use last-layer logits vs. truncated context scoring).

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), microbenchmark results, PRs.
